evidence_quotes.quote: The public participation processes that are taking place in Spain as a result of the implementation of the Water Framework Directive (WFD) constitutes an important step forward toward the democratization of water management in Spain.
Se ha analizado también la documentación suministrada por los diversos organismos de cuenca
De manera más concreta se ha entrevistado a 8 personas, 3 de administraciones públicas con competencias en la gestión del agua, 2 representantes de usuarios tradicionales
La representación de cada uno de estos usos en los órganos participados de gestión es proporcional a la cantidad de agua que utilizan.
Como se ha señalado, en el presente texto la valoración de los procesos en curso se ha estructurado a partir de las tres modalidades de participación prescritas por la DMA
remite a una cierta impresión de que el alcance real de la participación puede acabar siendo bastante limitado

criterion_notes.c1: Fails Criterion 1 (and matches Exclusion Criterion 7): the paper examines public participation in river-basin water-resource planning (élaboration of River Basin Management Plans / Planes de Gestión de Cuenca under the EU Water Framework Directive) across Spain's river basin districts, not household or community drinking-water or sanitation service access. Urban water supply utilities ('abastecimientos urbanos') are mentioned only as one traditional concession-holding interest group alongside irrigators and hydropower operators in basin governance bodies.
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain wording of Criterion 2 but fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading. Under the plain/literal wording, the paper examines legal, administrative, institutional, and governance factors in water management (transposition and implementation of EU Water Framework Directive 2000/60/EC via Spanish Law 62/2003 modifying the Consolidated Water Law, Aarhus Convention Law 27/2006, River Basin Agencies / Confederaciones Hidrográficas, Committees of Competent Authorities, and institutional inertia favouring traditional concession holders). Under the narrow 2026-10-13 clarification, Criterion 2 is 'no' because these rules govern stakeholder information, consultation, and active participation in macro-level river basin hydrological planning rather than a rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community water or sanitation service access (such as eligibility, tenure/documentation, tariffs, administrative burden, enforcement/disconnection, or utility regulatory structure governing access). Overall full-text decision remains 'exclude' under both readings because Criteria 1 and 4 are 'no'.
criterion_notes.c3: Satisfies Criterion 3: qualitative empirical study combining documentary analysis of secondary workshop/observatory reports and 125 public-participation documents from the websites of all 18 Spanish river basin agencies with 8 exploratory key-informant interviews (3 water administration officials, 2 traditional water-user representatives, and 3 university/social-movement experts).
criterion_notes.c4: Fails Criterion 4: evaluates process governance outcomes—implementation delays against WFD schedules, public access to environmental planning documents ('acceso a la información'), volume of consultation submissions, stakeholder diversity in workshops, inter-administrative coordination, and institutional credibility—rather than any outcome measuring household or community water or sanitation service access, connection, availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion.
criterion_notes.c5: Satisfies Criterion 5: population and unit of analysis (public participation processes across Spain's 18 inter-community and intra-community river basin districts from 2004 to 2010, plus 8 interviewed key informants), exposure (WFD Article 14 participatory mandates interacting with pre-existing river-basin institutional structures), outcome (quality, calendar compliance, inclusiveness, and credibility of participatory basin planning), and study design (qualitative documentary analysis and exploratory interviews) are clearly identifiable.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish with an English title and abstract. Per Criterion 10, direct comprehension/translation from the provided Spanish full text is feasible and was performed by the screener for full-text assessment.

study_design: Qualitative comparative documentary analysis and exploratory key-informant interviews
population_and_sample: Public participation processes across 18 Spanish inter-community and intra-community river basin districts (125 basin-agency website documents and observatory reports analyzed) and 8 key informants interviewed (3 public water administration officials, 2 traditional water-user representatives, 3 academic/social-movement experts)
exposure: EU Water Framework Directive (Directive 2000/60/EC, Article 14) public participation mandates (information, public consultation, and active participation) and institutional inertia within Spanish river basin agencies
outcome: Implementation timing, inclusiveness, methodological quality, inter-administrative coordination, and stakeholder credibility of public participation processes in River Basin Management Plan elaboration
rationale: Excluded as E01 (Wrong topic; see Exclusion Criterion 7: water-resource studies unrelated to household or community service access). Although the article is an empirical qualitative assessment of legal and institutional governance processes in Spain (reviewing 125 basin-agency documents and 8 exploratory interviews on the implementation of EU Water Framework Directive public participation mandates), it investigates stakeholder participation in river-basin hydrological planning rather than household or community water or sanitation service access (c1 = no), examines basin-planning participation rules rather than rule-type mechanisms governing service access (c2 narrow = no, though c2 plain = yes), and reports no water or sanitation service access outcomes (c4 = no).
